lang.name: English
app.tagline: Make any video buttery-smooth. AI adds in-between frames for a higher frame rate, right on your NVIDIA GPU. Offline · No quality loss · No account needed.
update.dl: ⬆️ Version {v} is downloading in the background: {pct}%
update.failed: ⬆️ Version {v} is downloaded but could not be installed (the app folder was in use): press Update to try again, or
update.btn.tip: Restart into the new version now. Left alone, it installs at the next start.
update.auto.tip: On: a new version downloads in the background and installs at the next start, or when you press the Update button. Off: this notice and its link only.
update.off: ⬆️ Version {v} is out (automatic update is off in this copy: {why}):
update.why.list: it has no list of its own files
update.why.locked: Windows does not let the app change its folder; move SmoothMyVideo to a folder you own
update.why.unpack: its unpacker could not run, an antivirus may block it
mode.video.tip: Smooth a video file and save the result
mode.live.tip: Smooth any window on screen in real time
pick.none: No file selected. You can also drag a video onto the window.
welcome.title: 👋 Welcome to Smooth My Video
welcome.body:
Drop a video on this window or click Select video… above.
You get a smoother, higher-frame-rate copy next to the original.
live.intro: Smooth any window live: a video player, a browser, a windowed game, with the model and Speed below. Click Smooth It Live!, then the window during the countdown, or press ` in any app. Windowed or borderless only; ` or Stop ends it.
live.fit.tip: Whole screen: everything on the monitor, with every model (DLSS 4.5 too). Original size: the window as it is. Fill screen: the window enlarged to its whole monitor, aspect kept.
live.key.tip: Toggles Live on the window in front, from any app (reserved while SMV runs). Click, then press a key or combo; Esc cancels.
live.unavail: Live needs engine/live/smv-live.exe, which this build lacks. Reinstalling the full app restores it.
order.note: Numbered panels are the processing order: each frame goes through them top to bottom.
nr.intro: Opt-in. NVIDIA's Neural Rendering redraws each frame with more photoreal light and surfaces; the generated frames inherit it. On an HDR screen it works on the window's SDR range.
nr.tip: Version: NVIDIA DLSS 5 Neural Rendering 310.9.16, NVIDIA's default model. Motion vectors: NVIDIA Optical Flow at Slow, its highest quality level.
nr.name: NVIDIA DLSS 5
nr.style0.tip: NVIDIA's Default look: the lightest touch, closest to the source, no frame-to-frame smoothing (the app's default)
nr.style1.tip: NVIDIA's Natural look: the smoothest, cleanest picture
nr.style2.tip: NVIDIA's Cinematic look: keeps the most line and texture detail
nr.passes.tip: Runs DLSS 5 this many times a frame, each pass on the last one's result: a stronger effect at that many times the time and video memory.
nr.automask.tip: NVIDIA's automatic character mask: DLSS 5 finds the characters on screen and treats their skin on its own (Skin Structure). Off: the whole frame gets one treatment and Skin Structure does nothing.
nr.skin.tip: How strongly DLSS 5 reworks the skin its Auto mask finds: 0 leaves skin as it is, 2 doubles the effect. At 1.00 (the default) skin follows Structure Intensity, NVIDIA's own default.
nr.mask.tip: Preview only: shows where DLSS 5 changed the picture (bright = a big change). The render is unaffected.
interp.intro: in-between frames from the model below; none ticked = the source frames, the other panels still apply
dlssg.tip: Version: NVIDIA DLSS frame generation 310.9.16 through Streamline 2.14.16. The model is picked in the NVIDIA App (Graphics, DLSS Override - Model Presets, Frame Generation). Highest quality in SmoothMyVideo: Use 3D app setting, the default; Recommended, Preset A and Preset B give the same frames. Preset C, NVIDIA's lighter and faster model, lowers the quality here and renders files no faster. SmoothMyVideo runs no DLSS Super Resolution.
dlssg.name: NVIDIA DLSS 4.5
dlssg.hint: (AI frame generation from games, the fastest; the default on RTX 40 and 50; multi-pass for high fps targets)
gmfss.tip: Version: GMFSS_Fortuna, union model (GMFlow with Softmax Splatting)
gmfss.name: GMFSS
gmfss.hint: (AI, best quality for anime; heavy on the GPU. Too slow? Lower the DLSS mode above, or pickPick NVIDIA Optical Flow below)
rife.name: RIFE
rife.hint: (Real-Time Intermediate Flow Estimation: AI, fast, best for live action)
drba.name: DRBA
drba.hint: (anime pacing: characters keep their own timing and crisp poses while camera pans smooth fully)
nvof.tip: Version: NVIDIA Optical Flow API 5.0, run by the driver on the GPU's optical-flow engine. Quality: Slow, the engine's highest quality level.
nvof.name: NVIDIA Optical Flow
nvof.hint: (NVIDIA's optical-flow hardware: really high fps, light on the GPU, friendly to slower PCs; very fast motion goes soft)
fsrfg.tip: Version: AMD FSR 4.0.2 frame generation (FidelityFX SDK 2.4.0). Motion vectors: NVIDIA Optical Flow at Slow, its highest quality level.
fsrfg.name: AMD FSR 4
fsrfg.hint: (AI frame generation from games; multi-pass, each pass doubles the frame rate)
xefg.tip: Version: Intel XeSS-FG 1.3.1 with XeLL 1.3.2 (XeSS SDK 3.0.2). Motion vectors: NVIDIA Optical Flow at Slow, its highest quality level. On NVIDIA GPUs XeSS makes one frame per pass. In SMV's test on real footage (2x) it matched RIFE and scored above AMD FSR 4 and DLSS 4.5.
xefg.name: Intel XeSS-FG
xefg.hint: (Intel's AI frame generation from games; multi-pass, each pass doubles the frame rate)
fruc.tip: Version: NVIDIA NvOFFRUC from the Optical Flow SDK 5.0.7
fruc.name: NVIDIA Smooth Motion
fruc.hint: (NVIDIA's optical-flow hardware; multi-pass, each pass doubles the frame rate; the lowest quality, varies run to run)
speed.fps.tip: Output runs at this exact frame rate, whatever the source is (decimals allowed: 47.952 is exactly 2x a 23.976 source)
speed.screen.tip: Output matches this monitor's refresh rate
speed.stepper.tip: Target frames per second (steppers move by 1; type up to 3 decimals for an exact multiple of a fractional source rate)
gpufit.tip: On (default): targets the highest frame rate your GPU can hold, at the lowest latency. When the GPU or its memory runs short, Live makes fewer in-between frames (down to the source rate) so every frame still shows; file renders keep their exact fps. Off: everything runs as set; Live may skip frames.
gpufit.label: Fit to the GPU
restore.label: Real-ESRGAN
restore.hint: cleans noise & redraws linework (Real-ESRGAN, anime); can flatten fine texture; heavy: a large window can lower the frame rate
restoreaj.label: AnimeJaNai HD
restoreaj.tip: Version: AnimeJaNai HD V3.1 Balanced (SPAN, 2x) by the database, from mpv-upscale-2x_animejanai 3.9.0. Licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, non-commercial use only.
restoreaj.hint: cleans noise & redraws linework (AnimeJaNai, anime, a 2x model brought back to the frame's size); lighter on the GPU than Real-ESRGAN
restorea4k.label: Anime4K
restorea4k.tip: Version: Anime4K 4.0.1, Restore CNN UL (the largest of its restore models) with its de-ringing clamp (Clamp_Highlights). The line restore of Anime4K's Mode A: ticked together with the Anime4K upscaler, the two are that mode. Its weights are inside SmoothMyVideo.
restorea4k.hint: sharpens linework & removes compression blur (Anime4K, anime); light on the GPU, keeps the frame's size
up.intro: the output size; DLSS 5 and the interpolation run at itLive's size is what Display shows; the DLSS mode below is its speed
dlssmode.tip: Live's speed: every pass runs at this share of the window or screen, then the result is enlarged to fit. DLAA = the full size; lower = faster and softer.
dlssrange.tip: The working size's share, 1% to 100% (DLAA); the DLSS modes sit at 33, 50, 58 and 67%. A very small size is raised to 64 px on its short side (128 px wide with DLSS 5).
vsr.tip: Version: NVIDIA RTX Video Super Resolution 1.6.0 (RTX Video SDK). Quality: the slider below, 4 = Ultra, the highest of its levels (the default).
vsr.name: RTX Video Super Resolution
vsr.hint: (NVIDIA's AI upscaler, used when the Size is above the sourceFill screen or a DLSS mode below DLAA enlarges)
vsrq.tip: RTX VSR's quality level. 4 = Ultra, the highest (the default); a lower level costs less GPU time a frame: 3 about 3/4 of level 4's, 2 about 1/3, 1 about 1/4.
vsrq.label: Quality
fsrup.tip: Version: AMD FSR 4.1.2 upscaling (FidelityFX SDK 2.4.0). Motion vectors: NVIDIA Optical Flow at Slow, its highest quality level.
fsrup.name: AMD FSR 4.1
fsrup.hint: (AMD's AI upscaler, used when the Size is above the sourceFill screen or a DLSS mode below DLAA enlarges)
a4k.tip: Version: Anime4K 4.0.1, Upscale CNN x2 UL (the largest of its models) with its de-ringing clamp (Clamp_Highlights). It enlarges 2x per pass, as many passes as the Size needs (above 2x a second pass), then Lanczos fits the Size. Ticked together with Restore: Anime4K, the two are Anime4K's Mode A. In SMV's fidelity test (1.5x and 2x, four clips) it came closer on average to the full-size original than RTX VSR and AMD FSR.
a4kaa.name: A+A
a4kaa.tip: Version: Anime4K 4.0.1, Mode A+A: after the first 2x pass, Restore CNN UL runs again on the enlarged frame, before the next pass or the final resize. Anime4K's notes: the highest perceptual quality and the most rebuilt lines, but it can add ringing, banding or aliasing, and it is slower (that second Restore works on 4x the pixels). Meant for enlarging 2x or more; with Restore: Anime4K ticked too, it is the full A+A chain.
a4k.name: Anime4K
a4k.hint: (a CNN upscaler made for anime, used when the Size is above the sourceFill screen or a DLSS mode below DLAA enlarges)
acn.tip: Version: ArtCNN 1.6.2, C4F32_DN (its denoising model) on the brightness, the colour from Lanczos. It enlarges 2x per pass, as many passes as the Size needs (above 2x a second pass), then Lanczos fits the Size. In SMV's anime test (2x, four clips) it came closest on average to the full-size original, ahead of Anime4K, Lanczos, RTX VSR and AMD FSR.
acn.name: ArtCNN
acn.hint: (a CNN upscaler trained on anime, used when the Size is above the sourceFill screen or a DLSS mode below DLAA enlarges)
xess.tip: Version: Intel XeSS-SR 2.0.2 (XeSS SDK 3.0.2). Motion vectors: NVIDIA Optical Flow at Slow, its highest quality level. In SMV's anime test (2x, four clips) it came last on average, behind ArtCNN, Anime4K, Lanczos, RTX VSR and AMD FSR.
xess.name: Intel XeSS
xess.hint: (Intel's AI upscaler, used when the Size is above the sourceFill screen or a DLSS mode below DLAA enlarges)
xess.howto: Intel's XeSS runtime is not included in SmoothMyVideo. Download Intel XeSS fetches Intel's XeSS SDK {ver} from {link} ({mb} MB), checks it and installs its runtime files (Intel Simplified Software License).
sharpen.tip: Version: Adaptive Sharpen by bacondither, the DX11 two-pass HQ version of 2021-09-10
sharpen.label: Adaptive (crisper picture)
hdr.intro: Opt-in. NVIDIA RTX HDR turns SDR into HDR, with its colour controls; Dolby Vision and HDR10+ below can add metadata to it.
rtxhdr.tip: Version: NVIDIA RTX HDR (TrueHDR) 1.1.0 (RTX Video SDK)
rtxhdr.name: RTX HDR
hdr.peak.tip: The brightest white of the HDR file, in nits (400 to 2000). Empty = the maximum of the HDR display this window is on
hdr.pure: (NVIDIA's RTX HDR look: Contrast 0, Saturation 0; brightness peaks at your HDR display's maximum)
hdr.vibnote: (Saturation boost: the whole image evenly; Intensity: muted colours only, vivid colours and skin stay)
dv.intro: Opt-in. Adds Dolby Vision metadata to the HDR render (open-source dovi_tool). For LG, Sony and most streaming boxes; not Samsung TVs. Profile 8.1 keeps the HDR10 video, which other TVs play as HDR10. Profile 8.4 writes the video as HLG, which other HDR TVs play as HDR and SDR TVs show close to right.
dv.81: Add Dolby Vision Profile 8.1 (HDR10 video, works with HDR10+)
dv.84: Add Dolby Vision Profile 8.4 (HLG video, up to 1000 nits)
dv.legal: Dolby Vision metadata is generated by the third-party open-source dovi_tool. Not affiliated with, endorsed by, or certified by Dolby Laboratories; "Dolby" and "Dolby Vision" are their trademarks.
hp.intro: Opt-in. Adds HDR10+ metadata (SMPTE ST 2094-40) to the HDR10 render (open-source hdr10plus_tool); still plain HDR10 elsewhere. For Samsung and other HDR10+ TVs; works beside Dolby Vision 8.1 in one file, not with 8.4 (its HLG video).
hp.legal: HDR10+ metadata is injected by the third-party open-source hdr10plus_tool. Not affiliated with, endorsed by, or certified by HDR10+ Technologies, LLC; "HDR10+" is their trademark.
out.intro: the file written from the passes above
out.av1: AV1 · GPU · royalty-free, best for web playback
out.vvc: H.266 · VVC · CPU · much smaller file, slow
prev.hint: your restore / sharpen / HDR settings on a real frame · updates automatically
cmp.tip: Shows the model ticked under Interpolate next to another model on the same moment: the real frames before and after on the left, each model's new frames between them on the right
cmp.hint: your model next to another one on the same moment
cmp.back.tip: The new frame before this one
cmp.fwd.tip: The new frame after this one
cmp.save.tip: Saves the four panes as you see them, with their labels, as a PNG
cmp.clip.tip: Saves one second from this moment as a lossless video of the four panes: every frame, real and new, with its labels, at the output frame rate (step through it frame by frame in a player such as mpv)
run.cancel.tip: Stops this render and deletes its progress (no resume). To continue later, Pause or close the app instead.
run.playprev.tip: Plays what is rendered so far, with sound and subtitles; made each time you Pause.
run.live.tip: The frame being written right now
run.livetoggle.tip: Shows or hides the frame being written; hidden, the engine stops making it (a little less GPU and CPU).
speed.round.tip: Round to {n}× of the source ({fps} fps): the closest whole multiple, on-grid real frames
run.resume.tip: Continues the interrupted render from where it left off (~{pct}% is already done). You can pause or close the app again at any time and resume later.
run.status.interrupted: Interrupted render found: click Resume to continue from ~{pct}%.
run.go.tip: Starts the render. You can pause or even close the app mid-render: it resumes where it left off.
run.status.ready: Ready. Pick a target fps, then click Smooth It!
run.status.select: Select a video, then click Smooth It!
rtxhdr.srcHdr: (source is already HDR, carried through as-is)
up.same: source is already exactly at that height, 1:1, nothing to resize
up.load: load a video to preview the result
codec.hevc.hint: safest choice: TVs, phones, editors and players all take it; audio is copied
codec.av1.hint: 1.4 to 1.6x faster than HEVC, higher fidelity; up to 2.5x larger on noisy content; plays in browsers, not on most pre-2020 devices
codec.vvc.hint: smallest files (about half of HEVC), slow CPU encode; plays in mpv, MPC-HC, MPC-BE and VLC 4, not browsers or most TVs
rtx.installed: The RTX Video runtime is installed.
rtx.noBridge: The RTX bridge (rtxvideo_cuda.dll) is missing from engine/rtxvideo. Rebuild it (see DEVELOPMENT.md, "Building the native bridges").
rtx.howto: Click Get from NVIDIA, then Choose .zip… and pick the downloaded RTX_Video_SDK….zip. It installs automatically.
rtx.pickAgain: Pick the downloaded RTX_Video_SDK….zip again with Choose .zip….
nr.line.sr: {file} (DLSS SR runtime from the same pack, optional)
nr.noBridge: The DLSS 5 bridge (nvngx.dll) is missing from engine/dlssnr. Rebuild it (see DEVELOPMENT.md, "Building the native components").
nr.howto: NVIDIA does not publish nvngx_dlssnr.dll (no SDK, no driver copy, no NVIDIA App override); it only ships inside NBA 2K27. Download the DLSS 5 runtime fetches the community build every DLSS 5 tool uses ({mb} MB zip from {link}, RTX 40 + 50), verifies its checksum and installs it.
aj.howto: AnimeJaNai is the work of the database, shared under {licence} (non-commercial use only), so SmoothMyVideo does not include it. Download AnimeJaNai fetches the author's release from {link} ({mb} MB archive), checks it and installs the model.
aj.unverified: The installed model is not the verified AnimeJaNai HD V3.1 Balanced (SHA256 {sha}…); it may still work.
dl.retry: Check the connection and try again.
fruc.intro: NVIDIA Smooth Motion uses NVIDIA's Optical Flow runtime (a one-time download, not bundled).
fruc.noBridge: The bridge (nvoffruc_bridge.dll) is missing from engine/nvoffruc. Build it once (see DEVELOPMENT.md, "Building the native bridges").
fruc.howto: Click Get from NVIDIA, then Choose .zip… and pick the downloaded Optical_Flow_SDK….zip. It installs automatically. Until then GMFSS is used.
fruc.lastStep: NvOFFRUC.dll installed. Last step: build nvoffruc_bridge.dll into engine/nvoffruc once (see DEVELOPMENT.md, "Building the native bridges"). Until then GMFSS is used.
dlssg.incomplete: The bundled DLSS runtime is incomplete: {files} missing from engine/dlssg. Reinstall the app (or rebuild per DEVELOPMENT.md). Until then GMFSS is used.
lv.effectsOnly: effects only ({restore}, {up}, {nr}, {sharpen}, {hdr}) at the source rate, capped by the {fps} fps Speed setting; tick a model to smooth
up.live.monitor: {whole} captures the screen as the player shows it, already stretched by the player's own scaler, so the upscaler never gets the video's real frames (at DLAA it has nothing to enlarge and stays off). For a video at its best: play it in a window at its own size (100%, e.g. 1280x720 for 720p), pick that window and set {display} to {fill}.
up.live.window: {orig} at DLAA keeps the window's size, so the upscaler has nothing to enlarge and stays off; {fill} enlarges the window to its monitor through the upscaler.
lv.fixed: the first whole multiple of the captured rate that reaches {fps} fps
lv.fixed.dlssg: (multi-pass past its one-pass limit, full passes first)
lv.load.rife: starts in ~3s (~45s the first time at a new window size)
lv.load.drba: starts in ~3s (~55s the first time at a new window size)
lv.load.gmfss: loads in ~4s (~30s the first time at a new window size)
lv.note.rifedrba: adds one source frame of delay
lv.fit.fill: enlarges the window to fill its monitor, aspect kept
lv.fit.monitor: smooths everything on the monitor the window is on
lv.key.fail: could not register {key} (taken by another app?)
lv.clickWindow: click the window you want smoothed…
lv.lost1: DLSS 4.5 back to {n}×: the second pass ended ({why})
lv.lost2: DLSS 4.5 back to {n}×: the second and third passes ended ({why})
lv.noWindow: no smoothable window was focused - click the window you want smoothed during the countdown
dvhp.mkv: (skipped for this video: its tracks need MKV output, {name} needs MP4)
dv.installed: The Dolby Vision export tool is installed.
dv.howto: dovi_tool is quietvoid's open-source tool (MIT licence) and is not included in SmoothMyVideo. Download dovi_tool fetches its Windows x64 build {ver} from {link} ({mb} MB), checks it and installs it.
hp.installed: The HDR10+ export tool is installed.
hp.howto: hdr10plus_tool is quietvoid's open-source tool (MIT licence) and is not included in SmoothMyVideo. Download hdr10plus_tool fetches its Windows x64 build {ver} from {link} ({mb} MB), checks it and installs it.
prev.note.mask: DLSS 5 changed {pct}% of the pixels, average change {mean}/255 · bright = large change, dark = untouched
prev.note.quick: quick preview shown; refining to the full RTX VSR/HDR/DLSS 5 version…
prev.note.srcHdr: source is already HDR (shown tonemapped); RTX HDR does not apply
prev.note.none: no Restore, Sharpen, DLSS 5 or RTX HDR enabled, the output will match the source
prev.note.plainDown: plain downscale, both panes match (RTX VSR is for upscaling)
prev.note.plainUp: plain upscale, no AI detail added (enable RTX VSR for that; both panes match)
prev.note.hdr: HDR is tonemapped to show on this SDR screen
prev.note.subtle: detail changes are subtle when the frame is shrunk to fit
cmp.needModel: Tick a model under Interpolate first: Compare shows it next to another model
cmp.running: running both models on this moment… the first run at a new video size takes up to a minute
cmp.note.resample: shown at {m}×, your target resamples between these
cmp.note.zoom: click to zoom (1:1, 2×, 4×) · hold Space to swap the two models
clip.running: saving the clip: running both models on {pairs} pairs…
err.fpsRange: Enter a target fps between {min} and {max}.
err.oneX: A 1× target adds no frames (output fps = source fps). Raise the target above {fps} fps to smooth, or turn off Interpolate to just sharpen / re-encode.
err.nothing: Nothing to do: turn on Interpolate, pick an Upscale resolution, enable Sharpen, Restore or DLSS 5, or turn on RTX HDR (and install its runtime).
run.pause.tip: Pauses the render. You can also just close the app - the render resumes where it left off next time.
run.resumeNow.tip: Continues rendering now. Closing the app instead is also fine - the render resumes where it left off next time.
run.status.paused: Paused; click Resume to continue (or close the app and resume another time).
run.status.prevReady: Paused. A preview of the part rendered so far (with sound & subtitles) is ready - click "Play preview".
run.status.prevPending: Paused; preview not ready yet (too few frames rendered) - Resume, then Pause again a bit later.
run.status.preempted: Stopped: DLSS was preempted (RTX Video). ~{pct}% saved - close the video and click Resume.
